chapter: Jazz at the Philharmonic and the record business
title: The badly pressed Modern records
summary: Gitler asks about off-center pressings of 'Mop-Mop' and 'Intersection'; McGhee blames poor California recording.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: What about the things on Modern that when they came out, they were pressed very badly, and I remember all the reviews said that their pressings were off-center and this and that...? Because I had heard them and I liked what I heard, but my pressing was also bad. "Intersection" and "Mop-Mop" and all of those...
Oh yeah, yeah.
What happened? Was that with strings?
No.
It was a bigger band, though, wasn't it?
No, it was just a band...
It was just a small group?
A small group.
For some reason I thought it was a bigger band.
No, it wasn't a big band.
What happened to those?
What do you mean what happened to them?
Did you ever get...
I got paid.
No... Did you ever get copies of them that were really playable?
Yeah, I got some here -- if I can find them.
I know I got 'em on tape here somewhere.

"Stardust," "Mop-Mop," "Intersection," and I'm trying to think of the fourth title. But whatever, we can look it up later. But those are something I never really heard correctly. And what I heard, I liked, but it was just not... It was off-center.
Well, that's because they didn't know how to record too well out there, you know.
Well, this is more the pressing, I think, than the recording.

Well, hah, that's one of the problems, too. But they didn't know how to make records out there. That was the country folks. Every time I think about California, I think how lucky I was to escape from there.
